fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Verse 1 opens with a rule about death for the priests, but verse 2 gives exceptions right away: his immediate family. So it isn't every dead person. The list is short, and God spells it out.

That's right, baker. God tells Moses that a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person among his people. Then verse 2 starts a short list of exceptions. So the opening rule is the starting point, and the exceptions are part of the picture too.

That's it, baker. Verse 6 says they present to the LORD the food offerings, the food of their God, and that's why "they must be holy." Think about handing someone a cookie box for a big celebration. I'm wiping the chocolate off my mustache first. Handling something that belongs to God is a much bigger deal than that.

You've got it, baker. Verse 12 says the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him, and verse 10 says that oil was poured on his head. Flour on my hat only means I've been working. This oil means God set him apart. That's the reason the text gives for not leaving or desecrating the sanctuary.

That's right, baker. Verse 22 says he may eat the most holy food of his God as well as the holy food. He can't offer it, but he's still allowed to eat it. He's still one of Aaron's family, and that's the part of this passage I'd hate for you to miss.

You've got it, baker. Verse 23 says that because of his defect, he must not go near the veil or approach the altar, so as not to desecrate God's sanctuaries. Then God adds, "For I am the LORD who sanctifies them." The reason comes from God's own words.

A fire guess makes sense next to an altar, friend, but this verse doesn't mention the fire. Verse 23 gives the reason as not desecrating God's sanctuaries. Then God adds, "For I am the LORD who sanctifies them." The answer is about the sanctuaries.

That's a kind thought, baker, and we all need a rest sometimes. But the text doesn't give rest as the reason. Verse 23 says he must not go near the veil or approach the altar, so as not to desecrate God's sanctuaries. The reason is the sanctuaries, and I won't add one that God didn't say.

The Levites make a fair guess, baker, since Numbers 3:6 has the tribe of Levi presented to Aaron the priest to serve him. But verse 24 doesn't name them. It says Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites. That's everyone, not just one group.
